subject: Canary fallout on edge routing — SLA confirmation, evidence request, and next steps
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@marketpay.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-04T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Spike in 503s during your canary this morning — timestamps & ask

Hi Grace,

Heads up — we saw a sudden spike of 503s and elevated tail latency during what appears to be a Redwood canary this morning. Our telemetry shows a sharp degradation starting ~2027-12-04T04:22:15Z and recovering ~2027-12-04T04:28:40Z (UTC). Rough impact: ~6m window, 1.8% of requests returned 503, and P99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s.

This affected our payment routing and caused several failed tokenizations; we had to route traffic to our fallback provider for ~10 minutes.

Can you please:
- Confirm the exact Redwood service window you see for elevated errors/503s (timestamps in UTC),
- Confirm whether this qualifies for an SLA review/credit per our contract, and
- Provide raw logs or a download link for the edge nodes that served traffic during that window (we need to reconcile request ids).

I attached a short snippet from our side showing the failed request IDs and timestamps.

We'd like to avoid opening a formal ticket yet — just collecting evidence so we can decide on next steps. If you can confirm the window and share logs, that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Sara Li
Head of Integrations — MarketPay
Attachments: app-error-20271204.txt

Folks — forwarding MarketPay's note. They reported a 6m window of 503s during our canary rollout this morning. Request from MarketPay: exact outage window, raw edge logs, and an initial determination of SLA eligibility.

Dev: can you pull the edge-pop logs and the canary manifest for the deploy that went out at 04:20 UTC? Ethan: please verify whether the routing fallback we rolled had any capacity constraints or misconfig that could explain KV-cache misses.

Priority: customer is asking for timestamps and logs before we open a formal ticket. Please respond with the exact impacted window (UTC), a one-paragraph summary we can send them, and attach any raw bundles or links.

Grace O'Connor

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ethan_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-04T09:05:40-08:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Spike in 503s during your canary this morning — logs + preliminary analysis

On Fri, 2027-12-04 at 08:35 PST, Grace O'Connor wrote:
> Folks — forwarding MarketPay's note. They reported a 6m window of 503s during our canary rollout this morning.

Quick summary / what I pulled:
- Impacted window (server timestamps, UTC): 2027-12-04T04:22:15Z -> 2027-12-04T04:28:40Z (6m25s).
- Root cause (prelim): the canary deploy included an old routing policy that unintentionally routed ~0.2% of traffic to edge-pop-7 which was running an older backend build. That backend had a hot-key causing cache thrash and spike in backend latency leading to 503s.
- Affected nodes: edge-pop-7 (node IDs: ep7-82, ep7-87).

Attachments I just uploaded to the shared drive and attached here: edge-node-logs-20271204.zip (raw logs for ep7-82/87), canary-deploy-manifest.txt (the deploy config; contains the routing policy that was toggled).

Notes on SLA eligibility: the window is >5 minutes continuous degradation with client-observed 503s. Per our standard SLA (availability measured per customer per region), this looks like a candidate for a credit review. I'll add a short replication note in INF-2742.

Next steps I'm taking now:
- Confirm whether any autoscale or capacity alarm suppressed failover for those nodes (checking metrics),
- Extract request ids that match MarketPay's sample so we can cross-reference,
- Draft a concise customer-facing summary for Grace to send.

Will update in ~30-60m with direct links to the log bundle and a suggested customer reply.

— Dev
Senior SRE — Serving Runtime
Attachments: edge-node-logs-20271204.zip, canary-deploy-manifest.txt
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@marketpay.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, ethan_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-05T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 503s during your canary this morning — confirmation & next steps

Sara — thank you for the report and for the error snippet; we've completed an initial evidence pull. Summary below and next steps.

Impact window (confirmed, UTC): 2027-12-04T04:22:15Z — 2027-12-04T04:28:40Z (6m25s). During that interval, a canary routing policy rolled traffic to edge-pop-7 where a deprecated backend build experienced high cache-miss rates and returned 503s.

What we’ve shared:
- Raw logs: https://drive.redwood.com/marketpay/edge-logs-20271204 (edge-pop-7 raw bundle, includes request ids you sent)
- Deploy manifest: canary-deploy-manifest.txt (highlights the routing key that toggled)
- Jira for RCA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2742 (we'll update with postmortem draft)

SLA / credits: based on the window and the visible 503s, this is a candidate for a standard availability credit review under our contract. I'll open the formal SLA claim and escalate to the billing team; that process typically starts with an internal review (we verify logs + reconstruct request impact) and then we calculate pro-rata credits if the incident meets the SLA thresholds. I will not pre-commit a dollar amount yet — we will come back to you with the outcome of the credit evaluation within our timelines.

Timeline & immediate asks:
- RCA timeline: we will provide a preliminary RCA within 72 hours and a final postmortem within 10 business days.
- Please confirm whether you want Redwood to: a) proceed with the formal SLA claim on your behalf (we can file using your account id), or b) simply share the evidence bundle and let you file. Either is fine.
- If you’d like a 30-minute review call, propose a window and we will coordinate.

Apologies for the disruption — we recognize how important low-latency routing is for payment flows. We're treating this as high priority and will keep you updated as we complete the RCA.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
